b.answer:
Worked example: a Harvest Lane test sheet with three deliberately messy rows. One Update a Row module writes five clean columns.

tidy_name    startcase(lower(trim(1.name)))
phone_clean  if(substring(replace(1.phone; /[^0-9]/g; emptystring); 0; 1) = "0";
                "+234" + substring(replace(1.phone; /[^0-9]/g; emptystring); 1; 20);
                "+" + replace(1.phone; /[^0-9]/g; emptystring))
order_date   parseDate(trim(1.date_text); "DD/MM/YYYY")
price_num    parseNumber(replace(1.price_text; /[^0-9.]/g; emptystring))
price_show   "₦" + formatNumber(parseNumber(replace(1.price_text; /[^0-9.]/g; emptystring)); 0; "."; ",")
Messy input (name · phone · date · price)Clean output
" aDE bakare " · 0803 123 4567 · 06/10/2026 · ₦12,500Ade Bakare · +2348031234567 · 6 Oct 2026 · 12500 · ₦12,500
"TUNDE okafor" · +234-805-555-0101 · 15/10/2026 · N 9,000Tunde Okafor · +2348055550101 · 15 Oct 2026 · 9000 · ₦9,000
" chioma EZE" · (0701) 222 3333 · 02/11/2026 · 26500.00Chioma Eze · +2347012223333 · 2 Nov 2026 · 26500 · ₦26,500

Check: 06/10/2026 reads as 6 October, not 10 June; price_num is a number you can sum in the sheet; only price_show carries ₦ and commas.
mistakes: Calling parseDate without a format, so 06/10/2026 becomes 10 June.
Writing "YYYY-mm-DD" when formatting the date, which puts minutes where the month should be.
Saving the ₦-formatted price into the number column, so the sheet can't add it up.
Separating arguments with commas instead of semicolons, so Make rejects the formula.
b.pass: Three messy rows each have five correct outputs written back to the sheet: tidy name, +234 phone, a real date read day-first, a plain number, and a ₦ display price with commas.
b.redo: Send it back if fewer than three rows were tested, if any date is read month-first, or if the parsed price is still text.

s.answer:
Worked example: the Harvest Lane receipt from the solved problem, with the title fix. The only change is the first_name formula: trim, then strip a leading title, then take the first word.

first_name
ifempty(
  startcase(lower(get(split(trim(replace(trim(1.customer_name);
    /^(mr|mrs|miss|dr|chief)\.?\s+/i; emptystring)); " "); 1)));
  "there")

The trim comes first so leading spaces don't stop ^ matching the title. The ifempty gives "Hi there!" if nothing is left. delivery_day and receipt_text stay as in the solved problem (Sunday rule with d = 0, ifempty(1.delivery_window; "time to be confirmed")).

Testcreated_atNameWindowReceipt shows
T1 SaturdaySat 10 Oct" mrs ADEBAYO "afternoonHi Adebayo! … Delivery: Monday 12 Oct, afternoon.
T2 FridayFri 9 OctDr. Ngozi OkekemorningHi Ngozi! … Delivery: Saturday 10 Oct, morning.
T3 Blank windowWed 7 OctBola Ade(blank)Hi Bola! … Delivery: Thursday 8 Oct, time to be confirmed.
T4 TitleTue 6 OctChief Tunde BakareeveningHi Tunde! … Delivery: Wednesday 7 Oct, evening.
T5 No titleMon 5 Octchioma ezemorningHi Chioma! … Delivery: Tuesday 6 Oct, morning.

Each receipt also shows Total: ₦ with commas from formatNumber, while the total column stays a plain number. A one-order run costs 2 credits (the trigger check plus one Update a Row), however many functions you use.

Submit: the formula text, the five test rows and a screenshot of the filled receipt_text column (test names only).
mistakes: Running the title regex before trimming, so "  mrs ADEBAYO" keeps its title because of the leading spaces.
Testing only names without titles, so "Hi Mrs!" is never caught.
Comparing the weekday with "0" in one place and 0 in another, or using "dddd" instead of "d", so the Sunday check never fires.
Hard-coding "time to be confirmed" instead of using ifempty, so filled windows are overwritten.
s.pass: All four required tests (Saturday, Friday, blank window, with and without titles) are shown, and no receipt names a Sunday, greets a title, or leaves a blank window without "time to be confirmed".
s.redo: Send it back if a test case is missing, if any receipt still says "Hi Mrs!" or a Sunday date, or if the fix was done with extra modules instead of functions.

g.answer:
Worked example: the 1.4 website order JSON (HL-0051) in JSON · Parse JSON as module 1, plus two edited copies with one and three items.

map and join give the SKUs, but not the quantities beside them:

join(map(1.items; "sku"); ", ")   → TOM-CRATE, PEP-TATASHE-L

Pairing qty with sku needs get() for each position (positions start at 1), guarded by length():

{{get(1.items; 1.qty)}}× {{get(1.items; 1.sku)}}{{if(length(1.items) >= 2;
  ", " + get(1.items; 2).qty + "× " + get(1.items; 2).sku; emptystring)}}{{if(length(1.items) >= 3;
  ", " + get(1.items; 3).qty + "× " + get(1.items; 3).sku; emptystring)}} · ₦{{formatNumber(1.total; 0; "."; ",")}}
Test orderItemsSummary
1 item3 × ONI-BAG @ 4,000 + fee 1,5003× ONI-BAG · ₦13,500
2 items (HL-0051)2 × TOM-CRATE, 1 × PEP-TATASHE-L + fee2× TOM-CRATE, 1× PEP-TATASHE-L · ₦35,500
3 itemsthe above + 3 × ONI-BAG2× TOM-CRATE, 1× PEP-TATASHE-L, 3× ONI-BAG · ₦47,500

Functions vs iterators (two sentences). map, join and formatNumber handled the SKU list and the money in one field, but pairing each qty with its sku meant one hand-written block per position, which silently drops a fourth item. An iterator plus a text aggregator (2.4) writes "qty× sku" once per bundle, so it works for any number of items.

Submit: the formula, three screenshots of the result for the 1-, 2- and 3-item tests, and the two sentences.
mistakes: Using get(1.items; 0), which returns nothing because Make counts from 1.
Expecting map(1.items; "sku") to also carry the quantities.
Formatting the total inside the JSON or the sheet instead of only in the summary text.
Testing only the 2-item sample, so the formula breaks or adds a stray comma for 1 or 3 items.
g.pass: The summary is exactly right for a 1-item, a 2-item and a 3-item order, and two clear sentences explain what functions did well and why an iterator scales better.
g.redo: Send it back if any of the three tests is wrong or missing, if the total isn't formatted with ₦ and commas, or if the functions-vs-iterators sentences are missing.
